fatigue.label: Tiredness
fatigue.recognise: Tiredness can build up. Tell your team how much it affects your usual activities.
fatigue.action: New marked weakness, faintness or a severe headache needs an urgent call.

rash.label: Itchy skin or a mild rash
rash.recognise: Tell the team about a new rash so they can advise on skin care.
rash.action: Call urgently for spreading rash, blisters, peeling or sores in your mouth or eyes.

nausea.label: Feeling sick
nausea.recognise: Take your prescribed anti-sickness medicines as directed. Tell the team if they are not helping.
nausea.action: Call now if you keep vomiting or cannot keep fluids down.

hair.label: Hair loss
hair.recognise: Paclitaxel can cause substantial hair loss. Ask the team about scalp care and available support.

neuropathy.label: Tingling or numbness
neuropathy.recognise: Tell the team early about tingling in fingers or toes, trouble with buttons, or a change in balance.

hearing.label: Hearing changes
hearing.recognise: Tell the team promptly about ringing, muffled hearing or difficulty hearing after cisplatin.

lung.label: Lung inflammation (pneumonitis)
lung.recognise: New or worsening cough or shortness of breath, even if mild.
lung.action: Call the oncology team now. Call 112 or 999 for severe breathing difficulty.

gut.label: Bowel inflammation (colitis)
gut.recognise: More or looser stools than usual, tummy pain, mucus or blood in your stool.
gut.action: Call the oncology team now. Tell them how many stools you usually have and what has changed.

liver.label: Liver inflammation (hepatitis)
liver.recognise: Yellow eyes or skin, dark urine or pain under the right ribs. Blood tests can pick up a problem before you feel it.
liver.action: Call the oncology team now if you notice these changes.

endocrine.label: Hormone gland inflammation
endocrine.recognise: Unusual weakness, dizziness, a persistent headache or a major change in energy.
endocrine.action: Call the oncology team now. If you collapse, call 112 or 999.

diabetes.label: Sudden high blood sugar
diabetes.recognise: Very thirsty, passing lots of urine, feeling sick or breathing unusually fast.
diabetes.action: Seek urgent assessment. Call 112 or 999 for deep difficult breathing, confusion or collapse.

kidney.label: Kidney inflammation
kidney.recognise: Much less urine than usual, blood in your urine or new swelling. Changes may first show on a blood test.

cardiac.label: Heart inflammation (myocarditis)
cardiac.recognise: New chest pain, palpitations, unexplained shortness of breath or fainting.
cardiac.action: Seek urgent assessment. Call 112 or 999 for severe chest pain, severe breathlessness or collapse.

weakness.label: Muscle or nerve inflammation
weakness.recognise: New marked weakness, double vision, trouble holding your head up, swallowing or breathing.
weakness.action: Call the oncology team now. Call 112 or 999 if breathing or swallowing becomes difficult.

temp.label: Fever or infection
temp.recognise: A fever, shaking chills or suddenly feeling very unwell. Chemotherapy can lower infection-fighting white blood cells.
temp.action: Call oncology immediately, even with a normal temperature if you feel unwell. Follow your unit’s temperature limits.

infusion.label: Reaction during an infusion
infusion.recognise: Flushing, itching, dizziness, swelling or breathlessness while the drip is running.
infusion.action: Tell your nurse immediately. After leaving hospital, call 112 or 999 for throat swelling or severe breathing difficulty.
